metadata.source: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 & RBI Official Portal (rbi.org.in)
metadata.exam_weightage: Very High (8-12 Questions across Mains shifts)

history.recommended_by: Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (Hilton Young Commission) in 1926
history.enabling_act: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act II of 1934)
history.original_ownership: Privately held shareholders' bank with paid-up capital of ₹5 Crore
history.nationalisation_act: Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948
history.longest_serving_governor: Sir Benegal Rama Rau (July 1, 1949 to Jan 14, 1957 - 7.5 years)
history.only_pm_who_was_rbi_governor: Dr. Manmohan Singh (15th Governor, Sep 1982 to Jan 1985)
history.financial_year_change: Shifted from July-June to April-March starting from FY 2021-22 (transition year was July 2020 - March 2021, 9 months)

central_board_of_directors.constitution: Constituted under Section 8 of the RBI Act, 1934
central_board_of_directors.official_directors: 1 Governor and not more than 4 Deputy Governors (appointed by Central Govt under ACC)
central_board_of_directors.non_official_directors: 4 Directors nominated from 4 Local Boards; 10 Directors nominated by Central Govt from diverse fields; 2 Government Officials (usually Economic Affairs Secretary & Financial Services Secretary)
central_board_of_directors.term_of_office: Governor and Deputy Governors hold office for a period not exceeding 5 years (eligible for re-appointment); Non-official Directors hold office for 4 years

subsidiaries.name: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
subsidiaries.coverage: ₹5,00,000 (₹5 Lakh) per depositor per insured bank (principal + interest)

subsidiaries.name: Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Private Limited (BRBNMPL)
subsidiaries.function: Prints Indian Banknotes to augment production capacity

subsidiaries.name: Reserve Bank Information Technology Private Limited (ReBIT)
subsidiaries.function: Serves IT and cybersecurity needs and improves cyber resilience of Indian banking sector

subsidiaries.name: Indian Financial Technology and Allied Services (IFTAS)
subsidiaries.function: Designs, deploys and operates critical IT infrastructure for RBI & banks (e.g. INFINET, SFMS, Cloud services)

subsidiaries.name: Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH)
subsidiaries.function: Promotes innovation across the financial sector with frictionless credit initiative, Swanari, etc.

coin_mints.entity: Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Limited (SPMCIL) - 100% GoI owned

locations.identification_mark: Diamond shape under the year of issue
No mark below the year of issue
Round solid dot (•) below the year of issue

currency_regulations.maximum_banknote_denomination: ₹10,000 (under Section 24 of RBI Act, 1934; previously printed in 1938 and 1954, demonetised in 1978)
currency_regulations.one_rupee_note: Issued by Ministry of Finance, Government of India; bears signature of Finance Secretary (NOT RBI Governor); defined as currency under Coinage Act
currency_regulations.all_other_banknotes: Issued by RBI under Section 22 of RBI Act, 1934; bear signature of RBI Governor with promise clause
currency_regulations.legal_tender_coins_limit: Under Coinage Act 2011, coins of ₹1 and above are legal tender up to ₹1,000; 50 paise coins are legal tender up to ₹10

core_functions.title: Monetary Authority
core_functions.description: Formulates, implements, and monitors the monetary policy to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of growth.
core_functions.legal_provision: Preamble and Chapter III-F of RBI Act, 1934 (inserted by Finance Act, 2016)

core_functions.title: Regulator and Supervisor of Financial System
core_functions.description: Prescribes broad parameters of banking operations, licensing, branch expansion, liquidity of assets, and management supervision.
core_functions.legal_provision: Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and RBI Act, 1934

core_functions.title: Manager of Foreign Exchange
core_functions.description: Administers foreign exchange, facilitates external trade and payments, and promotes orderly development of the forex market.

core_functions.title: Issuer of Currency
core_functions.description: Has the sole right to issue banknotes in India (excluding one rupee notes). Destroys unfit currency notes.

core_functions.title: Banker and Debt Manager to Government
core_functions.description: Performs banking functions for Central and State Governments; manages public debt issues; provides Ways and Means Advances (WMA).

core_functions.title: Banker to Banks (Lender of Last Resort)
core_functions.description: Maintains banking accounts of scheduled banks, provides rediscounting, liquidity through repo/MSF, and acts as emergency lender.

core_functions.title: Regulator of Payment and Settlement Systems
core_functions.description: Authorises, regulates, and supervises payment systems like RTGS, NEFT, UPI, NACH, and card networks to ensure safe and efficient clearing.

exam_traps.trap: Thinking RBI was established under the Banking Regulation Act 1949.
exam_traps.fact: RBI was established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. Banking Regulation Act was passed later in 1949.

exam_traps.trap: Thinking ₹1 note bears the signature of the RBI Governor.
exam_traps.fact: ₹1 note is issued by Ministry of Finance, Government of India and bears the signature of the Finance Secretary.

exam_traps.trap: Thinking coins are minted by RBI.
exam_traps.fact: Coins are minted by the Government of India (SPMCIL). RBI only distributes coins as an agent of the Government.

exam_traps.trap: Thinking all 4 currency printing presses are owned by RBI.
exam_traps.fact: Only Mysuru and Salboni are owned by RBI (BRBNMPL). Nasik and Dewas are owned by Government of India (SPMCIL).

exam_traps.trap: Assuming the maximum denomination banknote RBI can ever issue is ₹2,000.
exam_traps.fact: Under Section 24 of the RBI Act 1934, RBI has statutory power to issue banknotes up to denomination ₹10,000.
